title: Input → Process → Output
opening: The computer changes “hello” to “HELLO” when you ask for capital letters. The word you typed is the input, the instruction is part of the process, and the letters on the screen are the output.

labels.comparisonIntro: The thought and recording process stay the same. Change whether the input includes a useful example and a reader’s question.
labels.practiceIntro: Describe what entered, what actually happened, and what came out. Then name the intended effect and one condition that could change the result.

labels.length: This full note is over 2,000 characters. Shorten it to save; all of your text stays here.
labels.sourceQuote:
To see how an interaction produces a result, separate what goes in, what happens to it and what comes out: Input → Process → Output. A ball arrives, you meet it with your racket, and it leaves on a different path. A thought comes to mind, you explain it through a real example, and you finish a video.
When the result differs from what you wanted, examine the input and the process. What did you start with? What happened to it? What actually came out? Compare that with the result you wanted, change the relevant part and observe what happens on the next attempt. This gives you somewhere to look instead of simply demanding a better output.
